---
title: "GasBrineBench"
subtitle: "Experimental thermodynamic data for gases in water and brines, standardized and checked against the source papers"
toc: false
---

GasBrineBench is a curated compilation of published experimental data for
seven gases (CO~2~, CH~4~, H~2~, N~2~, O~2~, C~2~H~6~ and C~3~H~8~) in water and in brines of
Na^+^, K^+^, Ca^2+^, Mg^2+^, Cl^−^ and SO~4~^2−^, from 238 to 773 K and 0.1 to 3,500 bar.

* **26,815 datapoints from 249 published works** in eleven property families: gas
  solubility, water content of the gas phase, a CO~2~ + CH~4~ + water family, brine
  density, density of CO~2~-loaded brine, viscosity, apparent molar heat capacity,
  osmotic coefficient, vapor-pressure ratio, enthalpy of dissolution and permittivity.
* **One format.** Every datapoint is converted to one set of units and to molalities of
  six ions per kilogram of water, and carries its source, a quality code, flags for every
  convention or caution, and the result of a comparison with its paper.
* **A supplementary tier** of 5,174 verified measurements that cannot be converted
  without a model, kept in the units of the paper.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}
## Quickest start

```python
import gasbrinebench as gbb
df  = gbb.load()               # default selection
fit = gbb.load(reliable=True)  # audited subset
```

Or open the [tour notebook in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/jmoortgat/GasBrineBench/blob/main/notebooks/gasbrinebench_tour.ipynb);
the first cell sets everything up.
:::
